# #1756: Patch: in-app navigation resets the scroll position
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Clicking an in-app link from the bottom of a long page — say the foot of the Collection or Replays list — opens the next screen already scrolled to where you were, so you land halfway down instead of at the top. The browser's own Back button correctly restores your position; it is only forward navigation that keeps the stale scroll. After the change each new screen starts at the top and Back still puts you back where you were.

## Why

`navigate()` is a bare `history.pushState`/`replaceState` plus a custom event (`apps/web/src/net/navigate.ts:24-35`), and `usePathname` re-renders on that event and on `popstate`. Nothing in `src/` calls `window.scrollTo` or touches `history.scrollRestoration` — every `scrollTop` use is element-level (SettingsPanel body, chat box, log list). `pushState` never resets the window's scroll and `popstate` restores it, so the asymmetry is real.

## Proposal

Scroll to the top on programmatic navigation (the custom event), not on `popstate`; a small `navigate.test.ts` covers both. `net/navigate.ts` currently has no test file.

## Where it lands

`apps/web/src/net/navigate.ts`, `apps/web/src/routes/nav.tsx` users unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Following an in-app link from a scrolled page lands at the top
- [ ] Browser Back/Forward still restores the prior position
- [ ] Element-level scrolling (log, chat, panels) is unaffected
- [ ] A test pins both behaviours

## Size and risks

Extra small — about twenty lines plus a test. One caution: a screen that mounts slowly must not fight a late `scrollTo`, so the reset should run with the route swap, not on a timer.
